Weather & Closures

WEATHER & CLOSURES.

Weather, access rules, and volcano conditions can change fast. Use this page to understand how closures and route adjustments are handled before departure.

Weather in East Java

East Java has a tropical climate with two distinct seasons: the dry season (April to October) and the rainy season (November to March). While tours are available year-round, weather conditions can impact visibility and accessibility.

Park Closures & Force Majeure

National parks like Bromo Tengger Semeru and Ijen Crater may close temporarily due to volcanic activity, toxic gas, earthquakes, landslides, floods, or maintenance. We monitor these closures closely and will inform you of any changes to your itinerary.

Compensation Principles

If JVTO cancels or significantly alters services due to events beyond reasonable control (Force Majeure), we may offer reasonable alternative arrangements of comparable value, JVTO Travel Credit covering the unused portion, or a partial/full cash refund net of non-recoverable expenses.
